Definition: neuter of an alternate form of G2909; (as noun) better, i.e. greater advantage:--better.
BiblicalUsage: Kreisson is the neuter form of the comparative "better," and it appears three times, each time weighing one thing against another. In 1 Corinthians 7:38 the man who gives his virgin in marriage does well, but he who gives her not does better; in 1 Corinthians 11:17 the Corinthians come together "not for the better, but for the worse"; and in Philippians 1:23 Paul says to depart and be with Christ is far better. The form κρεῖσσον sits under the lemma κρείττων, which is the companion word G2909.
TheologicalSignificance: What convinces me here is that Paul's use in Philippians 1:23 settles the question for me: to be with Christ is not merely better, it is far better, and that is the measure for every other comparison.
